The bug in `Text.expand_tabs` was that it used the base style of the `Text` object when expanding tabs into spaces, ignoring any specific styling applied to the tab character itself. Additionally, it modified the internal `_text` attribute directly, which bypassed the `plain` property setter and failed to update the `_length` attribute.

The fix involves:
1.  Identifying the style of the tab character by checking if its position falls within any existing spans of the `Text` part; otherwise, falling back to the part's base style.
2.  Using this identified `tab_style` when appending the expanded spaces to the result.
3.  Updating the tab character to a space using the `part.plain` setter, ensuring that the internal state (like length) is correctly updated.

These changes ensure that styling is preserved during tab expansion and that the internal state of the `Text` object remains consistent.
